Content: This tune tells the story of a musician who went to war
Off he went into battle to treat the wounded
Suddenly, a shell hit nearby. The blast threw him into darkness.
Hello? {PlayerName}. I know you can hear me. The whole train has changed drastically.
Lily is on the verge of losing control. Her fear might manifest in the form of monsters of flesh and form.
Stay sharp. If anything happens, I'll let you know through the intercom.
Monster... let it be me. Just me.
Alone... I've grown used to it.
{PlayerName}, it's Lily!
Ugh, the carriages got pulled apart! We've gotta catch up with her, quick!
Careful, Tacet Discords.
Don't come any closer to me!
I don't want to hurt anyone...
They all want you to live on. You have every right to reach for your own happiness.
But I've got nothing left... There's nowhere in this world that'd still have me...
{PlayerName}, look out. More Tacet Discords incoming!
Where am I...? Who am I? Where am I going? I feel so sad. I can't remember anything at all.
Don't be afraid, Miss Lily. We're all here with you...
You've carried this weight long enough, young lady.
The happiness you brought us is more than we ever dared to ask for.
It's time to wake from this dream...
Enough now, Lily. This must hurt so much...
Take our petals. This time, let us carry you home.
Miss Lily, don't hurt yourself anymore.
Thank you, Miss Lily. It was you who gave me the courage to take up an instrument again.
The blue night will pass, and the dawn we've been waiting for will rise.
Lily... Yes. That's my name.
Look. Even land scarred by war can bloom with flowers once again.
You've never been alone...
We'll always be right here with you...
Lily...
We're falling even further behind! {PlayerName}, Lily's in bad shape, and it's getting worse by the minute!
We have to move faster.
There's no time. Let's make this quick.
The conservatory door... {PlayerName}, we're almost there!
The wind... Where did it come from? Where are you taking me?
Just... one last step!
...Help... Help me...
M-monsters!
Miss... Miss Lily... I just... want to go home...
The train to the frontlines dropped him at the Fifth Sector
He walked along a path of ruins
The air thick with rust and disinfectants...
At a corner, he found two soldiers dozing off
"New recruit? Registration's over there," they said, like he was just another piece of rubble
Behind the bunker, a young nurse was patching up a female soldier
"Greetings. I'm ▇▇, the commander of this sector."
"You a medic? Heard you were a musician?"
He couldn't answer. Swept up by the orators' speeches, he had led his entire orchestra to enlist
Yet when real blood stained his hands, he realized this was nothing like he'd imagined
The female soldier pointed to the nurse: "▇▇, he's your problem now."
The musician followed the nurse to his quarters
That first night, he didn't sleep well
The shells hit loud and close, showering him with dust
Then, just before dawn, the fight broke out
The first soldier was young. His lips trembled, but he didn't cry
He patched him up, whispering: "It's alright. You're gonna be alright."
He pressed on. Cries for help came from every direction
At a crossroads, the Grim Reaper offered him two choices
There were more cries coming from the left
He ran left, repeating the choice he'd just made
The left—saved. But the right?
Did saving some mean abandoning the rest?
The cries from the right sounded more desperate
He arrived too late. The soldier lay staring, unblinking, at the sky
It was already midnight when he opened his eyes. Through the dense fog, a figure emerged
An enemy soldier. But without a word, he offered bandages
Before he left, the soldier asked: "You're that famous pianist, aren't you?"
Turns out, he was a musician too. The two talked through the night
From classical masterpieces to modern compositions, from their first instruments to their debut performances
As dawn crept in, the musician asked a question
"Why are we even fighting? We speak the same language. We love the same things..."
No one could answer him. Not the generals, not the politicians, not the Sentinel
The enemy soldier looked at him and said: "I don't know either. We were once the same people, after all."
"This war's like rain, every drop falling from the eaves spares no one's shoulders."
They made a promise to talk through music later
A harmonica from one side of the trenches, an answering guitar from the other
Gentle melodies drifting over barbed wire into the distance
The musician wrote a piece, hoping to perform it with that soldier once peace returned
But their secret was discovered. The officers call it "treason"
As the musician climbed the scaffold, he remembered the piece he wrote didn't have a name
And why not call it "The Dawn That Sheds Its Blue"
He wanted to tell his friend
The blue night will pass, and the dawn we've been waiting for will rise
You're alright. Just don't slow down now...
To find what they left behind for you.
You'll journey to a place far beyond where we could ever go.
And when that day comes, please lay a bunch of flowers for us once more.
Keep walking forward. To the place we could never reach.
You fought so hard to come this far. You should be proud of the person you've become.
No... I don't want to be alone anymore...
Miss Lily...
Nurse...
Doctor Lily...
Let's go home together.
To the left! No, no, the right... Why do the paths keep splitting?!
You receive a message from Yangyang
{PlayerName}, might you spare some time?
A merchant caravan outside Xuanfang Hold rescued a man not from these parts. He insists on speaking with a Black Shores representative. Says they're the only ones who can help him.
I've let Suisui know, too. She's going to use the Guild's connections to try to confirm his identity.
Wait for me. I'll come find you.
A man not from these parts?
Wonderful. I'll wait for you at Shaftpost Yard. See you soon.
I know of your ties to the Black Shores, so I thought you might be able to help him.
Wait for me. I'll come find you.
By the time we finish looking into this, Yangyang will probably have already left Xuanfang, huh...
Every goodbye just makes the next hello all the better. So let's focus on what's right in front of us, okay?
Again with this Somnoire thing? I always feel like there's something weird staring at me in there.
Don't get all twisted up about it, though! It might just be my imagination.
{PlayerName}, you should be close to the Somnoire gateway.
Communications will be affected once inside. From here on, you will be on your own. Please be careful.
Relax. {PlayerName} ain't alone. I still count, don't I?
Of course... I hope you both return safely.
We made it. Huh? Hold up, {PlayerName}, does this "door" look different to you?
Yeah... Abby, do you still feel like something's watching us?
A little. But I can't tell where it's coming from. Maybe I should hide in your Tacet Mark for now.
You arrive at the entrance to the Somnoire, only to find that the gateway has changed. With caution, you and Abby step inside.
This must be the pocket of the Somnoire Jedediah mentioned.
You came...
It's been a while.
Ivory Gatekeeper. I was about to try to contact you.
I heard from a Goldrunner that something unusual appeared here. Have you discovered anything?
Follow me. You shouldn't be here. I'll escort you out.
Hey, wait for me!
(Something isn't right about the way it's acting. Is the Somnoire anomaly affecting it?)
(I'll follow along for now to see where it takes me.)
Fight, fight, fight... Every day, the same hellish thing. I'm so tired of it all!
These voices... What's happening here?
They all said to run. Run...
But where would we even run? Do they think we can outrun this damn war?
We stayed quiet. We stayed ignorant. We followed orders...
We aimed our guns at each other. At strangers we'd never met.
There's no absolution for people like us. She has to die... she has to die...
Only her death... will stop the bigger disaster from hitting us.
...Damn it. Quiet. Just be quiet!
(These voices are closing in... This isn't right. It can't be the Ivory Gatekeeper...)
Not walking anymore?
That depends on you.
I told you. You shouldn't have come here. I'm the one who's walking you out.
Look, the way out of the Somnoire is just ahead. It's hidden in that battlefield. But you will need a key.
A key?
Your sword shouldn't be pointed at me. It should be pointed at "her," somewhere in that battlefield. The key is... to kill her...
Only by killing her... can you leave.
Hey! {PlayerName}? {PlayerName}... What happened?
(It vanished. What was that just now?)
Abby, did you see that white cat? Someone seemed to be impersonating it, using it to guide us here.
No. As soon as we arrived, our connection got cut off. Next thing I knew, I was already here.
(Was that just another one of the Somnoire's illusions? Or is someone pulling strings behind the scenes?)
I don't know what happened, but we gotta be careful going forward. I smell something rotten...
Better I stay in the backseat for now. But if something happens, I'll be there to help you.

You quickly realize that the white cat before you is an impostor. Yet even with its identity exposed, it remains perfectly composed, calmly explaining that it is here to lead you out. The exit lies ahead, it says, but you will need a key to reach it. And the key is to kill "her"—the woman waiting on the distant battlefield. With that, the white cat vanishes.
I'll tie this up quick.
I see the battlefield ahead. The smoke is getting thicker.
Would you lay the one you love down in the dirt?
On your feet, you greenhorned worms! From today, your weapons are your woman, your man, your everything. Treat 'em right.
More of 'em. More of the crazies... Here they come with their weapons...
No point in roll call anymore... I'm the only one left. I want to go home. I want to go home. I just want to go home!
White flowers. They look like the ones by the entrance...
Tacet Discords. Were they drawn here by the abnormal frequency too?
Promeus, you said we held the reins of progress in our hands.
So where are you now? War is a vehicle for change. We're fightin' for the "change" you promised us. Are you watching? Do you even see us?
Promeus... The voices are getting louder...
I've had as much as I can take. Home. I just want to go home.
They sent us here on a train. When will it come and take us back?
What is he muttering about?
Hard to make out. He looks like a New Federate, though.
This is bad. These voices are starting to eat into my mind. I can't keep going like this.
You receive a message from Shorekeeper.
{PlayerName}, I just sent the coordinates of the Somnoire's gateway to your Terminal.
Mm, if there's any progress...
Yes. I'll contact you if there's any progress.
All right, I'll go over the Tethys System data again and see if I can find anything new.
Pro... proma—no, no. Prome... Promeus?
Miss Yangyang, for your safety, please keep your distance.
That one's not all there, if you ask me.
...Damn it! Damn it! These damn voices just won't leave me alone!
Promeus, the Resonator War... Get it all out of my head!
You... you're from the Black Shores, right? Help me! Take me away from here. Home... take me home...
Please take Mr. Jedediah to the Ministry of War to rest. I'll check in later.
Was he the outsider you mentioned? What exactly happened here?
Yes. He says his name is Jedediah, a Goldrunner from the New Federation. My sister confirmed it through the Guild's network.
He says Goldrunners are adventurers who chase freedom across the New Federation.
They use "Dream Pathways" to enter the Somnoire in search of valuables to trade. On one of these "treasure hunts," he stumbled into a particularly bizarre pocket.
Could this involve a Nightmare Tacet Discord?
Hmm... I don't think so. He said when he came to, he was standing in the middle of a battlefield.
Later, when he was trying to find a way out, he came across a door. He opened it without thinking and somehow ended up in <te href=700032>Mengzhou</te>.
It seems he's had dealings with Bloom Bearers before. He was asking about them everywhere in the Hold. That's why I reached out to you.
Anything else?
What did Jedediah say before he lost control?
Let me think... Oh, right. He mentioned a name. Promeus, the New Federation's Sentinel. He said that was the name he kept hearing, over and over.
So he figured the pocket he stumbled into might've been a battlefield from the "Resonator War" years ago.
I see. I'll contact the Black Shores and have them help Jedediah get back to the New Federation.
(Well... an old war resurfacing again inside the Somnoire is something to pay attention to.)
(And Promeus. Why would a Sentinel be mentioned in something like this? Could It be connected to the war Jedediah spoke of?)
Well then, {PlayerName}... until the Black Shores takes over, I'll keep an eye on him for you.
You were thinking about Promeus and the Resonator War, weren't you? I can tell something about it is bothering you.
Yeah. From what I know of the Somnoire, things that happen there can't just be brushed off as dreams.
I have things handled here. You should go ahead and look into it.
Thank you, Yangyang.
I'll leave it to you, then.
I'm glad to help. But remember, you're just one person. Please be careful, and contact me if you run into anything unexpected.
Mr. Jedediah, please calm down.
Promeus?
And he heard voices in his head, just like what you saw just now...

You arrive at the agreed meeting place with Yangyang, only to find a man screaming in agony before collapsing into a deep sleep. Yangyang explains that he is Jedediah, a Goldrunner from the New Federation. Goldrunners often venture into the Somnoire through "Dream Pathways" in search of treasure. During his latest expedition, Jedediah wandered into a strange battlefield where soldiers cried out the name of Promeus. Suspecting it was a battlefield from the Resonator War in the Federated Cities, he pressed on until the soldiers' screams drove him to the brink of madness. In a delirious state, he pushed open a door and awoke in the Mengzhou Borderlands. Now, he seeks the Black Shores' help to return to the New Federation. Sensing something amiss within the Somnoire, you decide to investigate.
After parting with Yangyang, you find a quiet spot and open a channel to the Black Shores.
Indeed... Aalto will head to Xuanfang soon to assist the Goldrunner. In the meantime, we will step up our monitoring of the Somnoire.
How did ordinary people without Resonance Abilities win that war?
At first, the Resonators had the advantage. But then a substance called Inverse Tacetite appeared. It suppresses a Resonator's power.
Once that came into play, the scales began to shift. Eventually, the government forces gained the upper hand.
The Goldrunner mentioned the name Promeus. I'd like to know, whose side was It on?
One moment... That's strange. There's only one note about Promeus in Tethys's records.
That doesn't sit right...
This war seems more complicated than it looks.
A Sentinel's core logic is to "guide civilization" forward. They're supposed to act when the situation calls for it.
But there's no record of Promeus doing anything in the war? Did the monitoring registers not detect any change in Its activity?
None that I can see... But the New Federation is hostile to the Black Shores. They have deported many of our Bloom Bearers in the past.
In that case... I need your help with something. I need the coordinates of the nearest gateway into the Somnoire.
I want to see for myself what happened with Promeus and that war.
Do you need me to accompany you?
No need. Besides, if something does go wrong, I know you'll find a way to be there. I'll rest easy knowing you have things covered on this end.
As for the "Resonator War" you mentioned, we have analyzed Hsin's fragmented frequency and re-examined the Tethys System's data using that information.
We have some preliminary findings. Where would you like to start?
What's the New Federation like?
The New Federation is a technologically advanced region in Solaris. Its society values freedom and innovation above all.
But unlike other regions, Resonators there are strictly controlled by the government.
It was a war between ordinary people and Resonators.
The Federated Army, led by ordinary citizens, ultimately prevailed over the Resonator army. Since then, Resonators in the New Federation have faced unequal treatment.
"During the Resonator War, Promeus took no action."
And as a neutral organization, we are bound by treaty to keep our observation to a minimum.

You contact Shorekeeper, who informs you that Aalto will soon travel to Xuanfang to assist Jedediah. She has also uncovered information about the New Federation in the Tethys System's database. One detail stands out: Promeus, the New Federation's Sentinel, took no action during the Resonator War. This is at odds with what you know of Sentinels, whose core directive is to "guide civilization" forward. Surely, Promeus should have acted when the situation called for it. With more questions than answers, you turn to your only lead: the battlefield hidden within the Somnoire.
You receive a message from Yangyang
{PlayerName}, Mr. Jedediah has been settled in.
Don't worry, I'll make sure this Goldrunner is seen to before I leave.
Yes. My work here in Xuanfang is done. I will miss this place... but I was only assigned here temporarily. I cannot stay forever.
Yes. But a little time apart is just the beginning of our next reunion.
The bonds between people are a strange kind of wonder. Time doesn't wear them down, and distance doesn't shake them loose.
They'll never change. I believe we'll walk together again someday.
Until that day comes, let us take care of ourselves. Protect those around us. Do what we are meant to do.
Yes. Well then, best of luck with your investigation, {PlayerName}.
Leave?
Leave? You're going so suddenly?
But actually... I don't think I'll be staying in Jinzhou for long either.
Yangyang, what are you thinking...
So where will you go next?
So where will you go next?
Words like "friends" and "family" are the same way. Tomorrow, and every day after that... in Jinzhou, in Mengzhou, anywhere on Solaris...
I understand.
I believe our paths will cross again.
I understand. And I believe our paths will cross again, too.
I believe our paths will cross again, too. Until then, I'll take care of myself. You do the same.
Mr. Aalto also contacted me and said it will take a few more days for him to reach Xuanfang Hold.
Yangyang, what are you thinking...
Lately, the Streams have been bringing me more and more voices. I can feel them... urging me to do something.
Funny enough, it is a place I know well.
Let me guess. Mingting?
Let me guess. Mingting?
It feels like... something unseen at work? I can't explain it. Once, the Streams led me to Jinzhou. And now they're calling me to Mingting...
I don't know what's waiting for me there. But... I can't ignore the Streams. Every voice behind them belongs to someone in need.
But whatever happens, I'm part of Jinzhou. That will never change. So this time... Mm. Let's just say I'm taking some time off.
Baizhi keeps telling me to use up my leave. I don't even know how many days I've accumulated by now...
Is this goodbye, then?
Is this goodbye, then?
What about the Resonator War?
From what we know so far...
A train whistle pierces the air, silencing the voices that have been gnawing at your mind. Nearby, soldiers queue to board the train. You decide to follow them.
Divinity of Rinascita... Can you forgive my sins...
You here for the broadcast too?
You've been through a lot. I left a fragrance diffuser in your room. It might help you rest a little easier.
Good night, {PlayerName}.
...The voices finally stopped. {PlayerName}, are you alright?
Yeah... You?
All good here. But where are we? Wait, do you smell that? There's a strange type of fragrance on this train.
The door doesn't open. You decide to investigate the train itself.
You don't see the ground or any tracks. The train is floating as it moves through the air...
Hello there, {Male=mister;Female=ma'am}.
I just saw you get on. Are you the one Mama sent to pick me up?
Sorry, kid. I don't know your mom.
Oh. Guess it isn't this stop, either. Then it must be the next one. That's alright. Liam will be a good boy and wait here.
Mm-hmm. I'll just keep waiting here.
Can you tell me where we are?
Can you tell me where the train is headed?
Lemme think... I've never really thought about it. I just know this is where I'll find my mama.
Sorry, {Male=mister;Female=ma'am}. I should keep looking for the person my mama sent. Goodbye.
Alright, I won't keep you. I hope you find the person coming to get you.
So your name is Liam.
The rest don't matter to me one bit.
I don't know. All I know is this train is taking me to my mama. Can't remember much else.

You board the train, where a strange little boy greets you and asks if his mother sent you to fetch him. You ask him where you are, but he doesn't know. All he knows is that this train can take him to his mother.
♪ Dear passengers, welcome aboard. Please wait patiently in the lounge...
If you have any questions, walk down the carriage to the conservatory and speak with the conductor. Thank you for your cooperation.
The conservatory and the conductor... That fragrance seems to be coming from that direction as well. I should go take a look.
"Lost as we are in the oceans of this earthly realm, there is more than one way to rise."
"Cling to light and goodness, and even in the blackest waters, you shall find your ship."
That style feels awfully familiar...
You're quoting the Codex of the Deep.
Stay back! Don't come near me. I don't want my filth rubbing off on you.
Even if "she" says she can clean the stench of depravity from me, I know better. No one... can wash away what I've done.
Mad things I've done can't be undone. I've no right to walk through that door.
So I hold this Rinascitan scripture, pretending it means something. Pretending I'll be atoned if I have faith.
I'm a joke, aren't I? As if Imperator would allow a Federate whose hands are soaked in blood to set foot in Their ark.
So-called faith won't save me. "She" won't save me, either...
Hey, you wouldn't happen to be called Tom, would you?
No, I think you've got the wrong person.
I'm {PlayerName}.
That so? Then you shouldn't be standing here. The broadcast just called for a "Tom."
Everyone here's a Tom, far as I can tell. Don't know why, but that voice has a pull. Dragged me right over.
Truthfully, I hate my name. It's just too common.
Back in the Seventh Sector, I met plenty of Toms. There was the kid Tom—carried his schoolbooks everywhere he went.
The drunk Tom, always going on about his farm back home. And the dreamer Tom, holding onto a busted broomstick like it was a guitar, swearing he'd be a star someday...
Every last one of 'em died. That's why I hate the name. Every morning, the casualty list would have another Tom on it.
My buddies would see me and go, "Hey, Tom. You're still standing!"
Yeah. Still standing. One day I won't be. Just waiting for my name to show up on that list.
Do you know where we are?
Feels like a troop train shipping us off to the next war zone. I've already spent more time on these rattling boxes than I have on solid ground.
Only thing is, I feel like I'm forgetting a lot of things. There's this weight on my chest. Makes it hard to breathe.
Heavier than a shell, and hurts worse than a bullet.
I'm getting closer to that fragrance Abby was talking about.
And then... Haha, my little girl comes runnin' up. Grabs my hand. Begs me to play hopscotch with her.
So I scoop her up. And we laugh like two little birds chirping away.
You've already found your way home, Tom.
Home... yeah. I'm home.
You can rest now. May your soul wander no more.
Nice meeting you, {Male=sir;Female=ma'am}. Is there anything I can do for you?
No, I'm not actually...
You look like you're carrying something heavy. Why don't you sit down, and I'll make you a cup of tea.
How's that settling, {Male=sir;Female=ma'am}? I put a pinch of chamomile in there. It's good for quieting frayed nerves.
I feel much better. That's some good tea.
But you needn't be so formal with me...
Too stiff for your liking? I see... you're the type who prefers things a little more familiar.
Then let me introduce myself. I'm Lily, a psychotherapist with the army, and the conductor of this train for now. If anything's weighing on you, I'm here to listen.
That's right, soldier. Are you having trouble with your memory? Don't fret. We'll take it slow.
No, what I meant to say earlier is that I'm not a soldier from the Federated Cities. This is my first time on this train.
If you're standing in as conductor, maybe you have some answers. Besides, I can tell you're different from the others on board.
Easy, I'm not here to cause trouble. You can call me {PlayerName}. Before I got on this train, I walked through a battlefield.
Then I heard a whistle. I followed it and found myself here with the rest of the soldiers.
Sounds like something's gone wrong out there.
Come with me. I've got a feeling another soldier's been swallowed by their own "guilt."
I see it. Creek by my house. Little white bubbles floatin' on the water. I know it's my wife. She's down there, washin' the clothes.
Go on, Tom...
The army... so this train's military? And when you say army, you mean the Federated Cities, right?
Let's start with something simple. Can you recall your name?

Following the onboard announcement, you arrive at the Conservatory Carriage, where a soldier's prayer to return home drifts from within. Deeper inside, you witness the soldier transform into a lily before a young woman. Mistaking you for a fellow Resonator soldier, she invites you to sit. Her name is Lily, a military psychotherapist currently serving as the train's conductor. Believing you have lost your memory, she gives you an opportunity to explain who you really are. Before you can ask her more, a commotion erupts beyond the door. Lily asks you to follow her and investigate.
What "guilt" are these soldiers carrying?
It's a kind of brokenness that takes root in their minds after all the fighting...
{PlayerName}, stay close to me from here on. The ones consumed by their guilt... they're dangerous.
Stop... Stop it right now...
Make it stop! Make it stop! Someone stop this train! I won't go to another battlefield! I won't!
Don't worry. I've done this more times than I can count. I know how to handle it.
You—stay back! I don't wanna... I don't wanna get off this train!
Soldier. Look at me. Breathe. This train isn't taking you to another war. It's taking you home.
Look around. Listen. It's quiet, isn't it?
This train... is goin' home? I...
You can rest now. May your soul wander no more.
{PlayerName}, I imagine you've got questions. Based on what you told me earlier...
You're still alive, and you shouldn't be here. This is a Train of Souls.
(He's in a similar state as Jedediah was...）
No crackling fires. No thunder of shells. No voices calling roll. I promise you... you'll never hear those sounds again.

In the Lounge Carriage, you find a soldier pointing a gun at those around him, shouting, "Someone stop this train!" Fearing for Lily's safety, you try to stop her from approaching him. She simply shakes her head, assuring you that she has handled such incidents countless times. She then approaches the soldier and gently calms him. Just as before, he transforms into a lily before her eyes. No one around you seems surprised; the passengers simply disperse as though nothing happened. Lily turns to you and quietly explains, "You're still alive, and you shouldn't be here. This is a Train of Souls."
But you're different. I can tell what you're carrying isn't the same as these soldiers.
When I woke up after I died, I was already here. I had the same questions you do. What is this place? What is this train?
Then I realized it was carrying me through war zones. And it draws the dead aboard. One by one.
What about the lilies? Every soldier you touch becomes one. Is that your Forte?
I reckon it's something the train gave me. I was a medic in life. All I ever did was try to soothe the wounded. This isn't so different.
Over time, I noticed when a soul's wounds are fully healed, they transform. Into a lily.
So I keep doing it. The therapy. The praying, all of it. I want their souls to find peace.
Not at all. I appreciate you sharing.
♪ ... Attention, passengers. We will soon be arriving at the Station of the Lost...
A new stop. Come with me, {PlayerName}. There's something I want to show you. It'll help you understand this train a little better.
Maybe it's because they only remember pieces of their lives. But I remember everything. I was the first passenger on this train.
Forgive me. It's been a long time since I've spoken to someone alive. I'm out of practice. I've been rambling...
A Train of Souls? What do you mean by that?
Just what it sounds like. A train that carries the dead to their final rest.
The battlefield you crossed was a corner of the Resonator War. Everyone on this train, myself included, died in that war.
Pain. Despair. Hatred. All the things that fester out there have poisoned our <ano=residual frequencies>souls</ano>. They keep us from finding peace.
Sounds like the stories of a "ferry" carrying the souls of the dead across the river. That's why you call it a <te href=700038>Train of Souls</te>.

Lily answers your questions one by one. The battlefield you crossed was part of the Resonator War, and she and the other passengers all died in that conflict. Their lingering frequencies were tainted by the suffering and resentment of war, preventing their souls from finding peace. Unlike the other passengers, who retain only fragments of their memories, Lily remembers everything. She has discovered that the train travels endlessly between battlefields, drawing fallen soldiers aboard. As she did in life, she now tends to their psychological wounds, drawing on her experience as a military medic. In time, she has found that when a soul's trauma is fully healed, it transforms into a lily.

Whatever this place is, I believe you, {PlayerName}. You've been nothing but sincere with the souls on this train. You trusted me. So ask away.

You haven't been waiting long in the Lounge Carriage when Lily arrives to show you how to order dinner. Simply close your eyes and picture the food you want against the starry sky outside the window, and it will appear on the table before you. Lily marvels at the wonders of the world of the dead, giving you an opening to explain your own understanding of this place. You know it as the Somnoire, and you have come to investigate the anomalies within it. To uncover the truth, you need her help. Lily chooses to trust you.

You ask what caused the Resonator War, but Lily knows little about its origins. Before the conflict began, she was merely an ordinary perfumer, and all she could do was watch as the flames of war inexplicably reached her home. An announcement soon warns that dinner time is nearly over. As if suddenly remembering something, Lily takes out her diary and records her 727th day in the world of the dead. Having lost all sense of time, she has relied on these entries to keep track of the days. Your explanation of the Somnoire gives her pause. She crosses out "world of the dead" and replaces it with "Somnoire," then asks whether you would willingly lose yourself forever in a dream indistinguishable from reality. You shake your head. Lily gazes at you gently but offers no reply. After wishing each other good night, you return to your respective rooms.
Back already? Want to chat a little more? I've told you so much about myself, now it's your turn...
I'd love to hear stories from the world of the living.
(Tell her how you got here from Mengzhou.)
I see. So this Goldrunner friend of yours... has he recovered?
My friends are looking after him. He should be fine.
That's good to hear... as long as everyone's alright.
You've been through a lot. I left a fragrance diffuser in your room. It might help you rest a little easier.
Thank you. In all your time on this train, have you seen a white cat? Or heard anything about a "key" or a "guilty soul"?
Not that I recall. Are they connected to what you're looking into?
I can't say for certain yet. But I feel like someone's been trying to guide me to find something.
A key and a guilty soul... it makes me think of the twisted darkness these soldiers carry. What if this "guilty one" is some kind of vile monster?
Just like in the fairytales, it hides in the corner of the dream, pulling all the strings. The only way out is to kill it.
If such a monster exists, {PlayerName}, promise me you'll destroy it.
I promise you.
I'll make no promises until I know more.
Good. Then it's settled. Goodnight, {PlayerName}.
...I understand. This is only a guess, anyway. We'll cross that bridge if the monster really shows up.
Goodnight, {PlayerName}.
Come on over, friend. Let's share a drink together.
You've had enough.
I ain't drunk. I'm... I'm clearer than I've ever been. Huh? Stop, stand still, will ya? Stop swayin' like that.
Didn't think they'd have whiskey this good on a train. Hey, hey, you ever been to the Federated Cities?
Place never sleeps. Lights burn all night, callin' in dreamers, grifters, folks willin' to bet it all on a maybe.
Freedom. Progress. Change. They keep piling those pretty words up higher and higher.
Then, "KABOOM!" Whole thing came tumblin' down. Hahahaha... and I'll be damned if anyone knows why.
I mean, wouldn't that fella over there be plumb tuckered out? He's been bangin' away at that piano all day.
Nah. But I figured he must've been some sort of big-shot pianist before he ended up here.
Tell me somethin' I don't know. That girl's got more talent than you can shake a stick at. Music, dancin', cookin', paintin', card games, hand-to-hand combat...
You reckon she comes from one of those noble families? You know, the kind that makes their kids learn a bit of everything?
No way. She told us herself, she's just a small-town perfumer. No fancy background.
Well, that's odd. Where'd she pick up all those skills, then?
Do you know him?
Yeah. He barely talks to anyone.
Seen plenty like him in the ranks. These artist types get caught up in the grand talk of glory, duty, and all that. Next thing they know, they've signed up.
Only out here, they find out there ain't no "art" to war. Ah well...
Yep. He plays every single day, like he's tryin' to confess somethin' through the keys.
I figure he must've been some sort of big-shot pianist before he ended up in the ranks. Probably enlisted on a whim. Hell, I've seen plenty like that.
Shame, really. War ain't got no ear for art or music, and it sure ain't got no time for high-minded ideals.
Out here, we let the guns do the talkin'. These great artists picked the wrong place to make their stand.
Speakin' of which, I heard Miss Lily plays the piano, too.
Hello.
What's this tune you're playing?
The pianist says nothing. His hands move across the keys, striking one note after another. No one knows when he will stop.
The soldiers need their rest. Better head back to my room as well.
Whoa... So this bottle's where that fragrance is coming from. My head feels all clear now. It's super relaxing...
What a nice room Lily got us! She's too sweet.
Well, we are in the Somnoire, but I don't think she was lying. The frequencies on her and the soldiers were really faint.
Just like what you'd expect from the dead. Besides, she didn't seem out to get us, and she laid all her cards on the table.
If it's still bugging you, we can always message the Ivory and Ebony Gatekeepers on WavesLine.
Not worried about something watching us anymore?
Nah, I felt way better the second we got on the train. But it seems I can't follow you into the dreams Lily weaves.
That explains it...
No wonder you were so quiet.
I don't mind. Roleplaying's too complicated for me anyway. I'll just stay in your Tacet Mark and save us both the headache.
Abby, what do you make of everything Lily told us?
(Lily is the only one I can actually talk to on this train. And the things she told me...)

Back in your room, Abby notices that the fragrance from the diffuser seems to have a relaxing effect. You ask what Abby thinks of Lily's words. Abby agrees that this place is the Somnoire but sees no reason to believe Lily is lying. Hello, Ivory Gatekeeper?
I'm in the Somnoire right now.

I'm in the Somnoire right now.
Failed to send message

Lily said the train might stop when all the souls on board find peace.
Yeah, your call... Just let me know when you're sure she's trustworthy. I'll come say hi.
Abby, I think we should stay on board and help her lay these souls to rest.

You discover that your WavesLine messages have failed to send, and suspect that the Somnoire is interfering with communications. Hmm... where am I? Those noises outside...
Tacet Discords... Wait, where did everyone go?
I can't smell that comforting fragrance in the train anymore...
Something feels different in this carriage now.
Just what was that...
We are all sinners... We are all sinners...
Kill her... Kill her...
We are all sinners... We are all sinners...
Kill her... Kill her...
Drink... Drink it up...
Dreamers... grifters... they're all gone...
Freedom... change... tumblin' down, all of it... Hahaha...
These words...
Sounds like they're imitating the soldiers.
Strange. These Tacet Discords don't seem to want to hurt me. What could they be...?
These Tacet Discords sound just like the soldiers from earlier. Who is this "she" they keep mentioning?
I need to find Lily. She's the most unique soul on the train. She should know what happened.
...This again.
You've come, {PlayerName}.
Lily, there are Tacet Discords on the train. The soldiers have all disappeared. Do you know what happened?
I know. But don't you worry. Once you've fulfilled your mission, everything will be set right.
My mission?
Aren't you here to investigate the connection between the Resonator War and the Somnoire? You came to fix the anomaly here... Kill ▇▇, and all shall be well.
Only you...
{PlayerName}?
Lily, are you alright? There were Tacet Discords on the train...
Tacet Discords? What happened, {PlayerName}?
The stars out there are beautiful, aren't they? They say that after we die, we turn into stars, so the ones who love us can still see us when they look up.
But... why didn't the soldiers and I turn into stars? Is it because no one remembers us anymore?
That's not true...
Maybe the time you lived in just couldn't bear to let you go. It kept you close, so your loved ones don't even have to look up to find you.
Mm... that's a good way to put it, {PlayerName}. A gentle, white lie.
Look, that crimson starlight over there is burning like a flame. Do you remember the story I mentioned before?
Yes. In the story, there was a little scorpion who met a vicious beast one day.
Yes, and in its final moments, it began to think. Prayed, even: "How many lives have I hurt, just to end here, fallen and alone..."
"If only I'd let that beast eat me. It would've lived another day, and maybe nobody else would've had to die for it."
As if hearing the little scorpion's wish, god set its body ablaze, raising it into the sky to light up the dark night...
But I think to that little scorpion, sacrificing itself for everyone else's happiness, that joy must've outweighed the sorrow in the end.
That's enough...
Meow...
That's strange...
It must've been a nightmare. I had one, too, and now I can't get back to sleep. How about we chat for a bit, {PlayerName}?
The one about a train?
Running for its life, the scorpion accidentally fell into a well. And as much as it tried, it just couldn't climb out.
So it gave up?
I... don't know what to say about an ending like that.
Right. Happiness or sorrow... which one was this ending meant to leave us with?
Lily...

You arrive at the conservatory and sense something strange about Lily. But the feeling vanishes as quickly as it came. She greets you as usual, assuming you've had a nightmare just as she has, and leads you to the window, hoping for some company. Then, she resumes the story she left unfinished...
Can't see it?
Then... come a little closer.
Burning to the very end...

- Why... can't I move...
- Leads only to death... Thank you...
It's nothing. I was just wondering if you needed my help today. I did promise to assist you.
About that... I thought it over last night. I really shouldn't let the cruelty of war burden another innocent soul.
Besides, bringing peace to these soldiers is my duty, not yours.
It does involve me.
I've made up my mind to help.
I came here to resolve the anomaly in the Somnoire. Based on what I know, my investigation won't move forward until this train reaches its final stop.
That's why I want to help you lay these souls to rest. I'm not one to just stand by and watch.
Just think of it as a small favor from the living. It's the least I can do for the departed.
Alright, {PlayerName}. But if their memories ever become too heavy for you, please let me know.
The soul needing our help this time is Mr. Grimm. Have you had the chance to meet him yet?
He's been playing the piano in the lounge, right?
Yes. He's been like that ever since he boarded, never speaking a word to anyone.
Even now, with his station just ahead, he remains completely silent.
I'll let you uncap the perfume bottle this time. Whenever you're ready.
Did Mr. Grimm disappear?
No. He's right here.
Come in.
Good morning, {PlayerName}. What brings you here? Did you sleep well last night? Is your headache any better?
Last night, I...
The headache's gone now. Thank you for that room you prepared, and the fragrance diffuser.
It's just...
(Lily's the most unique soul on this train, and she hasn't shown me a single hint of hostility.)
(She made me tea to help my headache, and she's been honest about everything to this point, from the nature of this train to the souls turning into lilies...)
(Maybe that nightmare last night really was just random?)
It's just...? {PlayerName}, is something wrong? You're looking at me like you've just had a nightmare...

Following the broadcast's instructions, you find the room for the next stop and discover that the soul awaiting release is Mr. Grimm, the pianist from the Lounge Carriage. Lily had intended to handle this alone, unwilling to involve an innocent bystander or expose anyone else to the horrors of war. You explain that helping the departed find peace is your choice, and the least you can do as someone still alive. After a moment's thought, Lily agrees to let you help.
How can this be happening?
{PlayerName}, unlike Liam's dreamland, you're experiencing this one directly through its owner's eyes.
This has happened with other souls before. Perhaps Mr. Grimm's self-loathing runs so deep that he can't bear to face his own heart, so he simply gave up on himself.
No need to rush, {PlayerName}. We can go at your pace. Is there anything you want to do first?
I can't seem to remember a thing.
My head feels fuzzy.
It's Mr. Grimm's voice. His consciousness is still hiding inside this body, but he sounds weak.
He wants people to hear it. It's a piece dedicated to his friend.
Take your time. Since there's no one else here, I suppose... I'll be his audience.
Come on. Let's go help Mr. Grimm finish his farewell performance.
Piano... Performance... My farewell performance... I want them to hear it...
This voice is...
What is it, {PlayerName}?
He told me he has a farewell performance to finish.
...Tch, that's all I could make out before his voice faded away.

Upon entering the dreamland, you discover that, unlike in Liam's case, you are experiencing this dream directly through its owner's eyes. Lily suspects that something in Mr. Grimm's past has left him afraid to confront his own feelings. Soon, you hear another voice within the body you inhabit, faint, fragmented words that seem to come from Grimm himself. From them, you gather that he has one last farewell performance left to give.
Piano... I want to play it... That tune, I still remember it...
Good evening, everyone. It's a great honor to spend this beautiful night with all of you...
The next piece I'm going to play is dedicated to a dear friend of mine. Please enjoy... "The Dawn That Sheds Its Blue."
(Piano... Performance..)
(Making a sound out of it is easy enough, but to play like a true musician... What should I do now?)
It's alright. I know what to do.
You step onto the stage, and Grimm's inner voice grows clear enough to guide you through the performance as a musician.
I'm... in my own body now.
But where is he now? There's no lily here, which means he hasn't found peace yet. Did Mr. Grimm...?
Shh. Listen. The piano... it's coming from the lounge. Let's go take a look.
So that's how it is, so that's how it is!
Hahaha... All this time, I just sat at this piano, playing it over and OVER again!
But what's the point? They're all gone...
And I was the one who led them here. I got them killed! I took part in this war and hurt innocent people!
No one's ever gonna forgive me! NO ONE! And if that's the way of it...
Enough.
Stop it.
Please stop, Mr. Grimm. A musician should <color=RedD>treat his instrument with more care.</color>
I... I'm sorry, Miss Lily. But... please. As the audience to this song and this story... will you forgive me?
I knew it. You can't answer. How could someone like me ever be forgiven?
No, Mr. Grimm. We can't forgive you on behalf of those you've harmed. We're not them.
Yes. So, please, Mr. Grimm, keep playing. Your music has the power to save those who come after.
I'm still alive. I can carry your song and your story forward. So no one else has to live through the tragedy you did.
Those who came after... I...
Hey, old friend.
"The Dawn That Sheds Its Blue," huh... That's a good name. I'll start. Try to keep up, alright?
Mm. Looks like Mr. Grimm ended it himself. It all happened so fast.
{PlayerName}... You're yourself again. Did we already wake from the dream?
Atone for my sins with a few songs? Play medic? Don't make me laugh!
The wrongs you committed are real, but so is your resolve to make things right. We both felt that through your music.

The performance ends abruptly. You awaken to find yourself back in reality, but Grimm is nowhere to be seen. Lily is just as bewildered. Then, a frantic flurry of piano notes erupts from the Lounge Carriage. You and Lily rush over to find Mr. Grimm pouring his anguish into the keys. The dream has restored his memories, and he now understands that the piece he played tells the story of his own life.

Grimm cannot come to terms with the sins he has committed. You and Lily speak up to stop him from giving in to despair. He turns toward you both, his expression growing troubled when he sees Lily. He asks whether she could ever forgive him. Lily hesitates, and you step forward to offer your thoughts. Your words reach Grimm, giving Lily the opening she needs to weave an apparition of his old friend with her Forte. At last, the two reunite on that small stage and fulfill the promise they once made.
{PlayerName}, let's bring Mr. Grimm's lily back to where it belongs.
What's gotten into you today? You've been starin' at that piano for a good while now.
Don't it feel too quiet in here? Like there's a song missin' in the air...
Missing the piano, hm? If memory serves, Miss Lily plays. Why don't you ask—
I can play, yes. Just tell me what you'd like to hear, and I'll do my best to...
Now don't you go troubling Miss Lily when she's already got her hands full on this train.
Pay 'em no mind, Miss Lily. They're only teasin'...
"The enemy hides among us, wearing the faces of our brothers and sisters as they encroach on our homeland."
"We will make them pay! We'll give every drop of blood we have for the future of the Federated Cities!"
"Fight for yourselves! Fight for your children! Fight for the glory of our Federation!"
Those words... Did you hear them from the officer before you boarded?
Haha, so you've heard them too, Miss Lily. Yeah, the very words that fooled me into signing up. What about you, {Male=sir;Female=ma'am}?
I've never heard them before...
I'm here for other reasons.
Count yourself lucky. They set off fireworks, beat the war drums, and screamed those slogans at the top of their lungs.
In that kind of frenzy? I don't think anyone could avoid being infected by those carefully crafted words.
What's wrong, soldier?
Do you want to play the piano?
I... I don't know. Guess I just hate music. So much that I want to smash this damn piano to pieces.
My big brother was a musician. When we were kids, he'd always ask me to be his first listener. But I'm a Resonator, and he's an ordinary person.
When the war broke out, he got drafted into the Federal Army.
The day he left, I cried my eyes out. I even threatened to smash every instrument he owned, but he left anyway.
And then? Did you ever see him again?
No. That was the last time I saw him.
He wrote to me sometimes. Said he made a good friend on the battlefield. A pianist... from the enemy side.
They promised each other they'd perform together once peace returned. But then, I got drafted into the Resonator forces, and I never heard from him again.
(Could his brother be...)
My brother was a romantic through and through. Always buried too deep in his own world.
Harboring ideas like that... wasn't he afraid of bein' executed for "treason?"
I reckon... they were terrified. But the music, and their hope for peace, gave 'em the strength to face that fear.
Hope for peace, huh... I wonder if he's still alive out there.
Mr. Grimm, you may rest now. May your soul wander no more.
Thank you, {PlayerName}. When Mr. Grimm asked me that question, I couldn't bring myself to answer.
It was your words that gave him the strength to forgive himself.
It was your power that helped him finish his final performance.
I suppose that's why a living soul like me would be here.
It pales in comparison to the power of your words.
All I could ever give them was a fleeting dream, and dreams always come to an end.
Mm. I hope you can find a way out of here safely. And then, just as you said, carry their stories forward to save more in the future.
There's still some time before dinner. You might rest in the Lounge Carriage for a bit. I'll leave you to yourself, then.
Oh, and the broadcast announces each station as we arrive. If it's no trouble, and you'd like to keep going together, you could... keep an ear out for it.
I will.
And about this diary...
I've written down everything I've experienced on the train. I thought it might help you understand what life is like here, and the soldiers who've passed through.
Well... let's save the rest of your and Abby's story for dinner. We've still got plenty of time ahead of us.
But it's your personal diary...
Personal? Oh, don't fret about that. My days here are as plain as can be. Even if you read every page, you wouldn't find anything all that special.
I just figured, since we'll be spending time together, trust and understanding are the least we can offer each other.
Trust and understanding... Right. Abby, come say hello.
This is my first step in trusting you. Meet my partner, Abby. It usually stays inside my Tacet Mark.
That's right! Bet you know what Echoes are, right, Lily? Well, I'm one-of-a-kind among 'em!
So you've been inside {PlayerName} this whole time... Abby. That's a cute name.
C-Cute?! {PlayerName}, you hearing this? Who goes around calling this majestic force of nature that...
My gut tells me your trust isn't misplaced.
See you later, then.
I'll see you at dinner.

Lily thanks you for giving Mr. Grimm a chance to reconcile with himself. In return, she shares her diary, which contains valuable information about the train and its soldiers. "Day 728 in the Somnoire..."
"Somehow, I've come to accept the help of that living soul."
{Male=He's;Female=She's} growing accustomed to life on the train...
And putting {Male=his;Female=her} kindness to work.
Day 15 in the Somnoire.
I've started keeping a diary to keep track of time, the same way she does.
Time keeps moving forward, leaving more rooms on the train empty.

"Day 754 in the Somnoire..."
Day 28 in the Somnoire.
It's just the two of us left on this train.
That nightmare still finds me sometimes.
But there's another unusual dream too...
Am I dreaming again?
Meow...
(This cat is... unusual. Its color doesn't match either the Ivory or Ebony Gatekeeper.)
(Where is it leading me?)
(It disappeared...)
(Something's off. Why am I back in the passenger carriage? I just left here a moment ago.)
(Wait... the cat's footprints. They stop before this painting...)
(Is that... Lily?)
Are you alright, young miss?
I-I'm fine. Thank you. What's happening...? Why have our lives turned into this?
Why is everyone taking up arms? They were my neighbors just yesterday. Why are they pointing a gun at me now?
I'm sorry, miss. This is our reality now. The neighbors you knew yesterday are your enemies today—all 'cause you're a Resonator, and they aren't.
The Resonator War has begun in the Federated Cities...
What about you, sir?
I'm a soldier. Fightin's all I know how to do.
But aren't you afraid?

I can't bear to watch any more people die in front of me. I fight so that more people like you can live.
Fight...
So more people can live...

A painting on the wall offers a glimpse into Lily's past. Shortly after the war began, a soldier came to her aid and explained why they had to keep fighting: to protect others and give more people the chance to live.
This painting before you is not the same one from your memory.
This is Lily's past. What is that cat trying to show me?
The footprints lead toward another painting...
How are you feeling today? Can you try repeating after me? "Ah"... "Oh"...
Don't waste your time, Doctor Lily. It's been a month since this coward lost her voice when she panicked on the battlefield.
Please mind your tongue, Officer Herriman! They're my patients. I won't have you speak about them that way.
Alright, alright. Whatever you say, Doctor. Just finish your rounds and sign off on today's chart already.
These drawings on the wall... Are you trying to tell me something?
Are these monsters? Are you saying there were a lot of them out there?
How could that be...
...No. You mean to say they don't exist in the real world. Only you can see them.
Are we done here, Doctor? Time's a luxury we don't have. The next ward's waiting.

Lily becomes a psychotherapist in the army. During her rounds in the ward, she encounters a soldier who has lost her voice and keeps scribbling on the walls. You damn demons, to hell with your therapy! I don't want it! I want OUT! I want RELEASE! You hear me?!
SHUT UP! You patch us up so you can throw us right back out there! Quit playing games with our lives! GET THE HELL OUT!
I-I'm sorry...
Don't let their ravings get to you.
You're a doctor. Your job is to save lives. You keep fixing them until they have served their purpose.
Now, sign your name on today's report.
Mhm... it's not serious. See, Doctor? That's why I told you to keep your distance from these people. They're all unhinged.
Why... why did you...
Why? Hahaha... You see those tally marks I carved into the wall, Doc?! Every single one is a time you patched me up!
They just keep adding up! I can't take it anymore... So I'm gonna kill you. For all of us!
No... I was only trying to save—

Step aboard, Doctor. I'm sure your courage and spirit today will earn you endless praise for generations to come.

You're the real demons.

How 'bout a song, Miss Lily?
Huh? M-me...?
Come on, everyone! Clap along and give Miss Lily a beat!
Not good. It's that same pain from when I first entered the Somnoire.
I have to...
It's alright, {PlayerName}...
Grip it right here, and steady your aim...
But I'm scared...
Go get some rest, Doc. We'll keep an eye on him.

As you move forward, the conservatory begins to transform until the room becomes the battlefield of the past. You witness fragments of Lily's life among the soldiers on the front lines, followed by a haunting image of her holding a gun to herself amid the flames of war. Let's begin, {PlayerName}. Time to finish Mr. Grimm's final performance.
(I remember this painting looking different.)
(Was that... a nightmare? Why would I dream of killing Lily?)
Abby, did anyone come into our room last night?
♪ We will soon be arriving at the Station of Choice. Mr. Grimm, please proceed to Room 03 and prepare for arrival...
Maybe... We're arriving at the next station. Let's go find Lily.
Didn't notice a thing. Maybe your brain's cooking up nightmares 'cause you're all suspicious about this train and Lily?
Hey, {PlayerName}. Bad dream again? You were yelling your head off just now. I tried shaking you, but you just wouldn't wake up.
I'm okay. This wasn't like the other nightmares. I saw Lily's past. But right when it came down to it...
It's almost time for you two to lay the souls to rest.
But there haven't been any broadcasts today.

Some force pulled me out of the dreamland.

Abby, what time is it?
