Do you think it could've been Lily?
Hmm... don't think so. Lily's too soft for a stare that suffocating.
Then chances are, if something really is watching us, there's a fourth person hiding on this train.
Nope. It's almost time for you two to lay the souls to rest, but she's been staying in the conservatory.

You wake up to find yourself still in your room. After one nightmare after another, you realize that someone has been deliberately interfering with your thoughts. When you ask Abby about the time, it reminds you that you and Lily should be helping souls find peace. Yet the train is unusually quiet today. You soon understand why: only one soul remains aboard.
You and Abby decide to make Lily's final day as happy as possible.
The diffuser fell to the floor?
I noticed it when I woke up too. But nobody came into our room.
The fragrance diffuser lies on the floor. In all your days on the train, nothing like this has happened.
Watching the overturned diffuser, you feel somewhat uneasy.
I've never heard this train so quiet before...
The lounge... Nothing's changed, except how quiet it is now.
Yeah. No piano, no warm greetings, no Lily chatting with the soldiers.
They've finally found peace. I hope that means they're home now.
{PlayerName}, are we really gonna say goodbye to Lily? I just feel...
I know, Abby. I feel it, too. But... they're already dead.
Good morning, {PlayerName}. You've done so much for me lately. I'd have thought you might like to sleep in a little...
I turned off the broadcast. There's only one soul left, so we're in no rush.
Mm. It's time for me to join them and find my way home, too. Thank you so much for everything... Oh, where's Abby?
I suppose you can hear me right now, Abby? Thank you. Getting to know you both made me so happy. But there's one last favor I'd like to ask of you...
So, until this train reaches its final stop, please take over as the temporary conductor. Look after everything for me.
I should be the one thanking you. You taught me everything about this place. I'm grateful to have shared this journey with you.
I'm not much good at goodbyes either. What I really mean to say is...
I won't forget any of you.
Come now, don't make things so gloomy. For me, this isn't just a goodbye. It's a new beginning.
You said you'd take our stories out into the world. But if you tell them with a face like that, I don't reckon anyone will want to listen.
So... how about a smile? Like this...
May your soul wander no more. May you welcome a tomorrow of your own.
This is...
All this time, we've been praying for the departed. But at the very end, I thought to turn it around—a blessing from the departed to the living.
{PlayerName}, we talked before about how this train, and all of us who died here, might be tied to the anomaly you're investigating.
Now, into the dream one last time.
Lily...
I know you're the last soul.
Abby's not very good at goodbyes. There's a lot it still wants to tell you, but...
I understand.
Abby wants your last day to be a happy one!
You're familiar with life on this train now. You know where to get food, when the lights shut off at night...
And you know how to tend to the lilies we turn into.
These words...
Once I'm gone, perhaps all your answers will finally come to light. I truly hope you make it out of here safely and leave all of this behind.

Lily is the last remaining soul on the train, but you're not good at saying goodbye. Just as the silence grows heavy, she smiles and offers a peculiar prayer. She hopes you will find your way out safely and never again become entangled with the souls of the dead.
I didn't expect my dream to look like this.
Why is there nothing here?
We're not playing as anyone this time.
Maybe my wish has already been fulfilled. After all, we laid every last soul to rest, didn't we?
I failed to save most of them when I was alive. But after I died, I was given a second chance. And this time, I could make a difference.
So maybe there's simply nothing left for me to hold onto. Maybe we just wait here until the dream ends.
No...
There's another possibility.
Hm?
A blank canvas means endless possibilities. Maybe the Somnoire knows how much you love diarying, so it gave you a blank page.
Lily, this dream is your reward for saving all those lives. You can paint this world with whatever colors you choose.
A reward... I...
...But, the colors I want might be a little complicated. Back when I was a perfumer, I had a little dream.
If the war hadn't happened, I wanted to travel the world. Gather rare flowers, blend new scents, experience different cultures.
But I never once left the Federated Cities. My world was so small... just the town where I was born, and the battlefield where I died.
Even dreams need reality to anchor them, don't they? I've never seen the world outside, so even here, I can't imagine what it looks like.
Then let's take a trip.
I'll lend you those colors.
Lily, I'll lend you my dreams and the worlds I've seen. Use your Forte to weave a new dreamland of your own.
We'll travel there together. My memories can build the world you've always wanted to see.
(On my very last day in the Somnoire, I embarked on my first and final journey.)
The worlds you've seen...
Nothing happened here?

Lily's dream is nothing but a blank expanse. She explains that perhaps all her wishes have already been fulfilled, and there's nothing left in the world for her to hold on to. But you don't believe that has to be the case. You offer another interpretation: a blank canvas also means endless possibilities.

You encourage her to think of something she still longs to do, no matter how small. Lily recalls a dream from her days as a perfumer. Had the war never happened, she would have traveled the world, gathering flowers, experimenting with fragrances, and experiencing different cultures. You decide to share the world through your memories and help her fulfill that dream on one final journey.

Through {Male=his;Female=her} eyes, I finally saw the world. First came Jinzhou. {Male=He;Female=She} had lost {Male=his;Female=her} memory, but there were those who guided {Male=him;Female=her} forward.
But with me, {Male=he;Female=she} became the guide. I could tell how much {Male=he;Female=she} loved this place. {Male=He;Female=She} remembered every shop, every face.
Jinzhou's streets held a trace of each season: chilled desserts, steaming meals, falling petals, and old folks waiting for their children to return.
{Male=He;Female=She} told me the people here had weathered many wars, too. But their enemies were Tacet Discords...
...While mine were the ordinary people I once lived alongside.
Next came Rinascita. Gondolas glided across the water—I'd never seen anything so gracefully imagined.
After sharing a bite of cake, {Male=he;Female=she} put on a mask and led me to an open-air stage. {Male=He;Female=She} had a small wish, too.
A festival called the Carnevale, one {Male=he;Female=she} never got to enjoy because of duty.

{Male=He;Female=She} couldn't bring {Male=himself;Female=herself} to tell {Male=his;Female=her} friends. Some things were {Male=his;Female=hers} alone to carry. So {Male=he;Female=she} never let {Male=his;Female=her} guard down, not even for a moment.
{Male=He;Female=She} invited me to dance, but I was clumsy and kept stepping on {Male=his;Female=her} feet.
It wasn't until we left that I understood: the Carnevale brought people from all walks of life together in song, even when they believed different things.
So why couldn't the Resonators and ordinary people of the Federated Cities...?
Later, we reached Startorch Academy. Haunted by the war, I'd always assumed anything related to "science" was a weapon...
"Academy"... that word felt so distant. At the age when I should've been in school, I was learning to hold a gun instead.
They came from different places, carried different stories, but they all gathered here for the same hope.
I wanted to stay, but I could feel my time drawing near.
Later, {Male=he;Female=she} took me out on a motorbike, racing fast enough to catch a fading aurora.
{Male=He;Female=She} wanted me to try driving, as if it might help me hold onto the world's last bit of warmth. But my body was growing weaker.
Mengzhou. The place {Male=he;Female=she} came from. Under the night sky, Moon Lanterns drifted down the stream, melting into the glow of the Waking Moon Festival.
{Male=He;Female=She} showed me the lantern tradition—writing your happiest memory of the year on a lantern, then letting it float away.
I didn't want {Male=him;Female=her} to see mine, so I scrawled it in messy handwriting. Only I know what those few words said—
Thank you, {PlayerName}. This final journey made me very happy.
It struck me then. {Male=He;Female=She} was just like everyone else. With the same ordinary worries, the same ordinary thoughts...
In the end, I made {Male=him;Female=her} finish the dance with a plushie Echo. Though {Male=he;Female=she} insisted I take a turn dancing with one, too.
{Male=He;Female=She} encouraged me to look closer. So I reached out and touched a robot named "TARD-E."
Its shell felt cold, but it was nothing like a war machine.
Everything here was wonderful. The strange inventions, laughter spilling out of classrooms, students dreaming freely about tomorrow.

Drawing on your memories, Lily weaves a series of dreams that take you around the world. Together, you wander the streets of Jinzhou, dance on a stage in Ragunna, experience student life at Startorch Academy, chase the auroras across the frostlands, and finally celebrate the Waking Moon Festival in Xuanfang Hold. Before the dream ends, Lily writes a message on a Moon Lantern: "Thank you. This final journey made me very happy."
It's okay. Even if this dream is over, maybe there's another way to show you the real world...
This journey was more than enough for me. Now I know what the world really looks like. It's so much gentler than I ever imagined.
The people of Jinzhou and Mengzhou suffered from war just like us, but they knew what they were fighting for.
Protecting their home. See, such a simple thing, yet so powerful. For me, I... I still don't know what we were fighting for...
I admire the people of Rinascita. They had their differences, but they set it all aside to sing and dance together. Seems disagreement doesn't always need to end in bloodshed.
And at Startorch, no one cared where you came from. Only where you were going next.
If I could, I would've loved to see it all for real... To touch a flower. To speak without fear. To talk and laugh with those folks...
Sometimes I wondered, did this world hate me? Why was I the one caught in all that misery? Did I do something to deserve it?
Don't burden yourself with those thoughts.
You were just an ordinary girl dragged into a meaningless war. The war itself was wrong.
Then just close your eyes.
Thank you, {PlayerName}. You showed me there's still tenderness and beauty in this world.
This was the happiest day I've spent in the Somnoire. If only... it could have come... a little sooner...
Lily...
(Open your eyes.)
Shh... Did I scare you?
The anomaly you've been searching for is me.
You shared your dreams and the worlds you've seen... Now, it's my turn.
But... that's impossible now.
Looks like my dream ends here.
Don't worry, I won't turn into a lily before you finish. I'll hear every word you have to say. But if it's too hard to watch...
...I can promise you one thing. This world could never hate you.
The reason you came here is also me.

The dream fades, and you return to the train. Lily thanks you for giving her such a wonderful journey. As farewell draws near, she confesses that she envies the people in the places you visited. They all know what they are fighting for. You reassure her that she was never the one at fault, and that the blame lies with the war itself. As Lily grows weaker, you struggle to bear the thought of losing her. She gently covers your eyes with her fingers, asking you to close them for one final goodbye.

When her voice suddenly falls silent, the train is overcome by stillness. You open your eyes, but instead of the farewell you expected, you find Lily before you, her face twisted by something unknown.
Just keep walking... Everything I wanted to tell you is right there.
Doctor Lily. Take a seat...
Do I need to remind you of your crimes, Doctor? Surely you weren't naive enough to think this would go unnoticed.
A month ago, the military ordered you to sign discharge papers for the newly stationed troops. Instead, you went behind our backs and shipped them to the rear for recovery.
Doctor Lily, do you know what you've done?
As their doctor, I had to assess whether they were fit to be discharged. They were on the verge of Overclocking. They couldn't fight. Not for a while.
I was only doing my duty. I broke no rules.
Is that so? Tell me, Doctor, do you even understand what "rules" are?
Only the victors get to make the rules. And this war is past the point of stopping. Everyone will do whatever it takes to win.
Those soldiers aren't pawns to be sacrificed for the higher-ups' victory.
They have families, friends. People waiting for them, same as you.
Oh, I know that too, Doctor. But what does any of that have to do with winning?
It doesn't matter if they're innocent, or if they even know why they're fighting. The war moves forward, and it takes us all with it. All we can do is follow.
Of course, there's always a fool who thinks they are the exception... In this case, you, Doctor.
Then I'd rather be the fool you think I am, than go numb the way you have.
Then let me tell you something else, Doctor. Those soldiers you tried so hard to protect? An order came to intercept them on their way to the rear.
They're already en route to the Fifth Sector. Since you were so desperate to keep them safe... Why not go join them?
You...
The Fifth Sector... Why does that name sound familiar? Ah, yes, I remember. Did you know, Doctor? It holds the highest casualty rate in all the Federated Cities.
Very well. Time to deliver the verdict to the accused—Doctor Lily, Head of the <te href=700033>Mental Health Care Center</te> at the Federated Field Hospital.
Upon review of the evidence, you have been found to openly defy military orders and falsify official records during your term of service...
The sentence is as follows: given the demands of the war, effective immediately, you are to be reassigned to the Fifth Sector.

As of today, Doctor Lily, you are now an official Resonator soldier of the Federated Cities. I imagine the news of you joining them on the frontlines will bring great joy to those children you fought so hard to protect.
Just as you wished, you'll be keeping them company soon enough.

The scene shifts back to the war. Lily stands trial before the military in an interrogation room. She had once been ordered by her superiors to discharge a group of soldiers from medical care. Recognizing that they were on the verge of Overclocking and unfit to return to combat, she defied the order and sent them to the rear to recover, upholding her duty as a doctor. The military regarded her actions as blatant insubordination. Lily was found guilty and reassigned to the forces in the Federated Cities' Fifth Sector.
As you saw, the military found me guilty and shipped me off to the Fifth Sector.
November 10th. Clear skies. The Fifth Sector. The night before the assault...
The past you...
We're to launch an assault tomorrow, orders from the top. I wonder how everyone's holding up tonight...
I should go check on the wounded.
Train rolls in November 11th... Kid, don't tell me you still believe that ticket's gonna take you home.
Tomorrow hasn't come yet. So there's still room to hope, right?
Lemme guess. Some brass shoved that ticket in your hand before deployment and said, "Fight hard, soldier. There'll be a train waiting to take you home."
Every poor bastard here's got one. If you ask me, it ain't worth the paper it's printed on.
The Fifth Sector—nothing but an execution ground. This is where they dump the troublemakers and everyone they've given up on.
Charge forward and die, and they'll dress it up as a "hero's death." Turn back, and it's a court-martial for desertion.
Forward or back, makes no difference. Our fate was sealed the day they shipped us here.
You'd be better off figurin' out how to make it through tomorrow. Ah, Nurse, perfect timing. Maybe you can knock some sense into this one.
Please, you two. There's no use dwelling on this. Though Mr. Rogett's right about one thing: what matters now is the battle ahead.
You're both recovering nicely. Get some real rest while you still can.
Ah, Miss Lily. Good evening.
Good evening. It's been a few months since you arrived at the Fifth Sector. You've settled in well.
...Is that because of the harmonica?
Heh, borrowed it from the commander. I'm a musician, after all. Sometimes music is the only way I can let things out.
The pieces you played were lovely. And the choice of songs—there was something in them, almost like you were speaking to someone far away.
Eh? Miss Lily, so you already knew...
It's okay... no need to say more. You weren't passing intel. There's been no violation. You were simply enjoying music, weren't you?
Mm... Thank you, Miss Lily. When this war's over, I swear I won't give up music again. <color=RedD>I'll treasure my instrument.</color>
One more thing, I've taken you off tomorrow's roll. I'll be enough to accompany the team.
You've only just recovered, and we're short-staffed as it is. Aside from me, you're the most experienced when it comes to mental health care.
If I don't come back tomorrow... the soldiers will need you and the other doctors to carry that weight.
But that puts an awful lot of pressure on you...
Don't you worry about me. Our job is to keep every soldier alive as long as we possibly can. Even one more minute is worth fighting for, isn't it?
Yes... It's shameful. A young girl with more resolve than I've ever had.
Miss Lily, you really are something.
Good night, Mr. Grimm.
When the war's finally over, what are you gonna do?
Get drunk. Sleep tight... But honestly? I'm scared.
Scared of what?
That I won't fit into normal life ever again.
Hey, any of you know why we're even fighting this war?
Idiot. Somebody up top's making a fortune off it. That's for damn sure.
Don't look at me. I ain't one of 'em.
I know. None of us are.
Lily, there you are...
Yes... Just here for the usual update. The wounded are all recovering well. You can rest easy.
But to me, you'll always be a little girl.
He must get it from you, always pestering people for hugs. I wonder how he's doing on the train right now.
Worried about him? Then... you let it carry you through tomorrow. Don't you dare give up.
Thank you, Lily. If you hadn't looked after him on that train, I can't even imagine what could have happened to him...
You've also been the one holding this Fifth Sector together. Pulled us out of the fire time and again. I owe you everything.
But you did more than your job. Besides psychological care, you learned nursing, simple surgery from the other doctors. Things no one asked you to.
And you made a point of getting to know every soldier, so they'd feel safe with you. Word is, you've become quite the woman of many talents.
Lily, you really are something.
Something... No, I... Honestly, what's gotten into everyone tonight? You're the second person to say that to me.
Because it's true. And because you deserve to survive tomorrow.
Listen to me, Lily. You've never once fired a shot. Your hands are still "clean." When this war ends, you'll still have a life waiting for you...
So... if anything happens tomorrow, don't worry about us. Run. I don't care where. Just live. That's all that matters.
Stop, don't go jinxing us like that. We're all making it through tomorrow, same as always. Nothing's gonna go wrong.
Mm. You're right. We'll all come back safe. I've got to. Liam's still waiting for me on that train.
Look, I've written him dozens of letters. One for his tenth birthday, one for his twentieth, one for his thirtieth...
I hope they find their way to him, one by one, as he goes through life.
If I see Liam again, do you reckon he'll be angry with me? For lying to him all this time?
Haha! Oh, he'll pout, alright. Might even refuse to eat at the same table as you.
That's all right. If that happens, I'll just do what you do and hum that lullaby you taught him, wait until he falls asleep, and stay 'til he's ready to forgive me.
You're not wrong. I heard it's based on an old story. A living traveler boards a train bound for heaven by mistake, and spends the whole ride saying goodbye to everyone who's already gone.
He's so full of grief that he reaches for anything that might feel like "happiness" again. Then he wakes up, and realizes it was only a dream.
Funny thing is, even at the end, the story never really tells you what "happiness" actually is.
Not knowing what happiness is, yet still having to carry all that sorrow... It really is a strange story.
I only did what I should. I'm a doctor, after all.
Hm? Cassandra?
Look at you, have you been eating at all? I heard you've been running yourself ragged tending to the badly wounded.
They're out of harm's way now. Tonight, you put yourself first. Get some sleep.
Mm... Cassandra, could you let go of me first? You've got to stop treating me like some little girl.
Now that I think about it, is it really a lullaby? The first time I heard him play it on the train, there was a hint of sadness in it.

On the eve of the frontal assault, Lily gives Commander Cassandra her usual report on the wounded. Noticing how exhausted Lily looks, Cassandra urges her to get some rest, if only for tonight. She then thanks Lily on behalf of the Fifth Sector's soldiers, and as a mother herself, for protecting Liam aboard the train. If anything goes wrong tomorrow, she tells Lily, she must run, no matter where. Lily has never fired a shot at the enemy. Her hands are still "clean."

Lily asks Cassandra to stop talking as though the worst is bound to happen. Sitting back-to-back, the two begin imagining what life will be like when they're reunited with Liam. Their conversation brings to mind the lullaby Liam played on his harmonica, and Cassandra picks up where Lily leaves off, telling an old story about a train carrying the departed toward heaven...
November 11th. A day I will never forget...
Even now, I remember every single cry they let out.
Even now, I remember... the feel of every raindrop against my face.
Calm down, Lily. The battle's begun. You've seen scenes like this before, more times than you can count.
The formation's been broken up by the earlier bombardment. I need to find Cassandra.
The soldier before her lies silent, a train ticket still clutched in his hand.
The soldier's eyes stare straight into Lily's, yet his soul seems to have drifted somewhere far away.
Lily realizes he died in that pose to shield something clutched in his arms.
How could this happen... I can't let any more soldiers end up like them. Cassandra, where are you?
...Help... Help me...
Hold on, Paul. You're gonna be fine. I'll—
Miss... Miss Lily... I just... want to go home...
Let him go, Lily.
Ca-Cassandra...
He's gone. There are still wounded over there, waiting for you. Go.
Headquarters gave us bad intel. The enemy had reinforced the line with heavy weapons. We walked in blind.
Our squadron's losses this time... Damn it. Those bastards at HQ used us as guinea pigs just to measure the enemy's firepower.
M-monsters!
They've all turned into monsters!
Easy, soldier! Report, what's happening?
Tacet Discords... I saw our own dead rise up. Turn into monsters. They look just like Tacet Discords.
What?
All units, hold steady! Ready yourselves for battle!
Remember what I told you yesterday? If anything happens, you run. You're still young. You still have a future waiting for you.
Take this gun. And stay alive.
The kit... No, no, this won't be enough...
No... no... I'm not trying to ease your pain. I'm trying to save you!
Why... Why can't my Resonance Ability mend a body? Why... Why can't I do anything at all...!
Please... don't go with that peaceful look on your face. I want to save you. Save all of you! That's all I've been fighting for.
LILY, RUN!

By the time Lily rejoins her unit, the battle is already over. A gravely wounded soldier dies before her eyes, and while she is still reeling from the loss, another soldier cries out that their fallen comrades have turned into monsters. Moments later, the creatures emerge from the smoke. Cassandra presses a pistol into Lily's hand and orders her to run. Fear and unease spread across the battlefield, and as these emotions overwhelm Lily, she panics, stumbles to the ground, and loses consciousness.
Why...
Oh? The ability to weave a dream, even for an instant, and you'd let it go? How wasteful...
Oh... Awake now?
Easy, easy. Mm, you're perking up. One more cup of tea ought to finish the job.
Where am I?
The depths of the Somnoire, where consciousness and imagination meet. Though I prefer to call it the Dream Abode. Sounds more romantic, don't you think?
Meta, the Somnoire... Why am I here? And the s-soldiers—
Monsters... No. They're not monsters!
Oops. My mistake. Poor choice of words. How about I put it in a way you prefer... A war-born curse? Frequencies that got a little corrupted?
You Resonators are different from ordinary folks. You leave behind a frequency even after death.
And war? It's the perfect nest for fear and resentment. Only natural they'd end up looking like that.
Then why did you save me?
Save you...? I wouldn't call it that.
You used too much power on that battlefield. I thought it was the Somnoire leaking, so I scooped you all up and brought you here.
Asking if they can go back to normal? Hmm...
Would this deal save them?
You weave fleeting dreamlands to soothe people. I can grant you the power to make those dreams last, very nearly forever.
Then you can save them all. Let them sleep forever. No thoughts, no memories. Like dolls...
No, no... That's just lying to myself. They wouldn't really find peace that way.
Is that so bad? They'd still be "alive," wouldn't they? And practically eternal, too.
Eternal... Time. That's it. If I can use dreams, then at the very least, I'll have all the time I need.
Every perfumer knows a craft called "refinement." Perhaps I can learn from it. Draw out their corrupted frequencies.
Interesting. But once you extract that corruption, what then? You'll need somewhere to put it, won't you? It can be contained in a body, or be devoured by Tacet Discords. But in here...
Deal. What's your name?
Lily Grace.
And the cost? What price will I have to pay?
The cost? Why, isn't it obvious? You take in all that corruption, and in its place, you become the monster.
Lily. From this day on, our deal is in effect.
As for me, call me Meta. You might say I'm the owner of this place.
Shhh... Keep your voice down. Wake them up, and they'll turn right back into monsters.
But... here's the thing! After everything you've been through, not a single trace of those nasty frequencies stuck to you. You're still you.
Still myself... Then what about them?
Not in the waking world, of course. But we happen to be in the Somnoire! So... want to make a deal with me?
Oh? You already have a plan? Impressive, cooling that head of yours so quickly. So how would you put my power to use?
Then I'll be that vessel. I'll bear all the "curses," all the "corruption" myself.
Well? Frightened?
...When that day comes, please. Destroy me.
We'll cross that bridge when we get to it... If you're ready, push open the door behind you and step through. The dream you asked for is waiting. I'm dying to see whether you can work a miracle.
Of course, there's always a fool who thinks they're the exception... In this case, you, Doctor.
Take this gun. And stay alive.
Stay alive... Yes. I'll live on, for all of you.
And then... I'll embrace death.

When Lily awakens, she finds herself in an unfamiliar room, face-to-face with a colorful cat. The cat introduces itself as Meta, the owner of the Somnoire, and explains that Lily is now within its domain. Lily's Forte is connected to dreams, and her excessive use of it on the battlefield led Meta to mistake the disturbance for an outflow of the Somnoire's power. In response, Meta drew the entire battlefield into the realm.

Sensing Lily's desperate wish to save the soldiers, Meta proposes a bargain. It will lend her a portion of its power, allowing her to extract the corruption tainting the soldiers' souls. In exchange, Lily herself must become the vessel that contains it. Without hesitation, Lily agrees, asking Meta to destroy her if she ever becomes a monster.
I've gotten the hang of extracting those corrupted frequencies now. The first fallen soldier should be arriving any time...
Not sure it'll go quite as planned. Perhaps I should fix something to help them feel at ease.
Herbal tea ought to help. I'll brew it a little milder.
Mm... The vase suits this spot perfectly. I hope they like the scent.
This... is my diary. Before the war, back when I still worked in a conservatory, I used to write down the little things about my days.
Time flows differently here in the Somnoire. I'll need to keep that in mind. Perhaps this diary can help me track the days.
These old entries... They don't need to be here anymore. I should tear them out.
Cassandra...
I know. You don't remember me now. But that's alright. This time, I promise I'll protect you.
I... My child... Want to go home...
Don't you worry. I'll help you find Liam. I promise.
You can go home now.

Aren't you the least bit curious about the price?
{PlayerName}. A pleasure. I am the current owner of the Somnoire—Meta.
But wasn't it Lily who opened that gateway?

This is... my dream? Or something I truly lived? And that person...
